project.projectDesc: Explores customer characteristics associated with credit-card default using data analysis and logistic regression.

caseStudy.summary: This academic analysis explores customer characteristics associated with credit-card default using exploratory analysis and logistic regression. The repository is titled SQL/NoSQL, while its available notebooks focus on Python and R data analysis and modeling.
caseStudy.challenge: The project asks which customer characteristics are associated with default and how those relationships can be analyzed from a credit-card dataset. It needs data preparation, interpretable modeling, and evaluation views that expose both model behavior and class imbalance.
caseStudy.architecture: The notebooks load the UCI credit-card dataset, prepare features, perform exploratory analysis, and fit logistic regression. Precision-recall and ROC analyses are used to examine classification behavior.
caseStudy.diagram:
flowchart LR
  Dataset[UCI credit-card data] --> Prep[Cleaning and feature preparation]
  Prep --> EDA[Exploratory analysis]
  Prep --> Model[Logistic regression]
  Model --> Evaluation[Precision-recall and ROC analysis]
  EDA --> Findings[Customer characteristic findings]
  Evaluation --> Findings
contributions: Built Python notebooks using pandas and NumPy for dataset preparation and analysis.
Fit logistic regression and explored precision-recall and ROC evaluation.
Created R visual analyses using dplyr and ggplot2.
tradeoffs: Logistic regression provides an interpretable baseline but may not capture nonlinear relationships without additional features or models.
Precision-recall and ROC views offer complementary perspectives on a potentially imbalanced classification problem.
The README frames the coursework as SQL/NoSQL, while the available implementation primarily demonstrates Python/R analysis.
